stem.en: The neutron was discovered in 1932, long after the proton. Which property of the neutron best explains why it took so long?

text.en: It has no charge, so the charged plates that revealed electrons and protons do not bend it.
It sits outside the atom, too far away for the detectors of that time to reach.
It is much lighter than an electron, so it hits too softly to be noticed.

explanation.en: Electrons and protons were found because they bend between charged plates. A neutron has no charge, so it passes between the plates unbent, and it shows itself only when it hits something. It is not outside the atom: it is in the nucleus. It is not light either: its mass is about the same as a proton's, which is why it could knock protons out of wax.

hints.en: How was the electron found? It bent towards a positive plate. What would a particle with no charge do?
